system.summary: Period key sheet in the bundle: each plaintext letter has one digit and each digit stands for two or three letters (0 a/x, 1 d/p, 2 f/r, 3 b/h, 4 m/y, 5 e/l, 6 c/g/u, 7 i/n, 8 q/s, 9 o/t); words separated by spaces or dots; dots over digits not used by the key as read. The same sheet carries a letter-for-letter substitution (not treated).

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout set the protocol; a volunteer of the CGAunis photographed the bundle at the AD17; AI agents transcribed (two blind passes and a blind arbiter per letter, none of them shown the key), froze the key, ran the pre-registered measures and read.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout

solution.what: Key sheet ('mode d'emploi') of the same bundle, photo 20261126_162030: table 3 (plain letter -> digit) transcribed and frozen by SHA-256 before any decoding.
Letters A, B, C: two blind passes by agents without the key, blind arbiter (A 81 of 483 groups differed, B 36, C 116).

PREREG 1 on A p2.23-p3.08 (358 digits): share of groups segmenting into lexicon words, 200 permuted-key controls; 0.987 against 0.974, criterion >= 0.85 and >= best + 0.30 not met: the metric did not discriminate (2-3 letters per digit). Declared; portion burnt.

PREREG 2 on fresh portion A p1.01-p1.09 (40 groups of >= 4 digits), after a declared power check on the burnt portion (0.7255 vs 0.2745): exact lexicon form of >= 4 letters, 400 controls (200 permuted keys, 200 random keys of the same 2-3 letter structure); 0.85 against best 0.425 (mean 0.121); criterion >= 0.50 and >= best + 0.30 met.

Letter chosen in each digit's set by sense; A read in part (0.877 sure, 0.943 with probable words), B 0.891 sure, 0.953 with probable words after a blind sign plate; C decoded, not read (out-of-focus line starts).

Blind sign plate on letter B (blind/planche-2711/, rule hashed 033239a3... before any vignette, answers by Brice Dudout copied byte for byte): 3/3 controls; 4 of 5 target digits settled on the photograph (p1.09 4 -> 9 croire, p1.12 [9/4] -> 7 liure, p2.01 4 -> 5 quinse, p2.01 1 -> 7 iours); p2.06 [8/3] answered 8, no word. Letter B before: 254 words, 224 sure, 5 probable, 3 supplied, 22 unread (0.882 sure); plate only: 254 / 228 / 5 / 3 / 18 (0.898); with five readings by sense kept probable (no digit changed): 256 / 228 / 13 / 3 / 12 (0.891 sure, 0.953 by sense).

validation.notes: PREREG 2: 0.85 vs best of 400 controls 0.425 on held-out A p1.01-p1.09. PREREG 1 (different metric, A p2.23-p3.08) failed for lack of discrimination (0.987 vs 0.974) and is reported. The key is the period key sheet of the bundle.

outcome.fraction_read_source: sure words over cipher words of A and B (427 + 228 of 487 + 256 = 0.882); probable {x}, supplied [x] and unread ‹…› are holes. C is not counted (decoded, not read).

texts.label: Letter A, 26 May 1726, to M. de Boissiran at Saintes
texts.summary: 427 of 487 cipher words sure (0.877); with probable words 0.943. A woman's complaint against a 'dangerous' hypocrite who repeats what happens in the house, then estate business: the metayer, the metairie, a miller who burnt a mill (2,000 livres).

texts.label: Letter B, Bordeaux, 14 August 1725, to M. de Boissiran
texts.summary: 228 of 256 cipher words sure (0.891); 0.953 read by sense after a blind sign plate (4 digits settled, 3/3 controls). Intimate letter ('mon cher fils', 'mon cher ami'; relation not established): a ship to Marennes, a maidservant, cabbages and shoes, his procureur.

texts.label: Letter C, Bordeaux, July 1725
texts.summary: Decoded with the key; not read: line starts out of focus on the photographs.
